t.1.21.1: Then the bird, who could go wherever he wished, of great valor and great strength, came to his mother's side on the far shore of the great ocean.
t.1.21.2: There Vinatā, defeated in that wager, sorely afflicted with grief, was reduced to the state of a slave-woman.
t.1.21.4: There is a very lovely and delightful abode of the Nāgas, gentle lady, in a secluded spot in the belly of the ocean; carry me there, Vinatā.
t.1.21.3: Then one day, at a fitting time, Kadrū summoned the humble Vinatā in the presence of her son and spoke these words.
t.1.21.5: Then the mother of Suparṇa carried her, the mother of the serpents, and Garuḍa too, urged on by his mother's words, carried the serpents.
t.1.21.6: That bird, Vainateya, flew close to the sun, and the serpents, engulfed by the rays of the sun, fell senseless. Seeing her sons in that condition, Kadrū then praised Śakra.
t.1.21.7: Homage to you, lord of the gods of gods; homage to you, slayer of Bala! O slayer of Namuci, let there be homage to you, thousand-eyed one, lord of Śacī!
t.1.21.9: For you, O Puraṃdara, are able to pour forth abundant water; you alone are the cloud, you are the wind, you are the lightning-fire in the sky.
t.1.21.8: Be a raft of water for the serpents scorched by the sun; you alone are our supreme refuge, O best of the immortals.
t.1.21.10: You are the scatterer of clouds and their dense masses, and yet they call you the cloud itself. You are the matchless, dreadful thunderbolt; you are the roaring rain-cloud.
t.1.21.12: You are the great being, the wonder; you are the king, you are the highest of the gods. You are Viṣṇu, you are the thousand-eyed one, you are the god, you are the supreme refuge.
t.1.21.11: You alone are the creator of the worlds and their unconquered destroyer; you are the light of all beings, you are Āditya, you are Vibhāvasu.
t.1.21.13: You are all the amṛta, O god; you are Soma, supremely worshipped. You are the hour and the lunar day, you are the tiny instant, and you indeed are the moment.
t.1.21.14: You are the bright fortnight and the dark fortnight as well, the kalā, the kāṣṭhā and likewise the truṭi; you are the year and the seasons, the months, the nights and the days.
t.1.21.15: You are the supreme earth with its mountains and forests, and likewise the sky, free of darkness, with its sun; you are also the great ocean, abode of fishes, teeming with timis and timiṅgilas, full of mighty waves and many makaras.
t.1.21.16: Thinking “You are great glory,” the wise great seers ever worship you, and you, glad of heart, being praised by them, drink the soma at the sacrifice, and also the oblations offered with the cry of vaṣaṭ, for the welfare of all.
t.1.21.17: You are constantly worshipped here by the brahmins for the sake of rewards, and you are sung in the Vedāṅgas, O you whose flood of strength is unequalled. For your sake the foremost of the twice-born, devoted to sacrifice, master the Vedāṅgas together with all the Vedas.
